finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /restore passes attacker-supplied base64 directly to Marshal.load. Marshal deserialization of untrusted input can instantiate arbitrary loaded classes and run their marshal_load/_load/initialize side effects, which is remote code execution when a gadget chain is available in the loaded gems. Severity: critical if reachable.
finding.source: app.rb:6 params[:state] (POST form or query parameter, no authentication)

trace.note: post "/restore" route, no before filter or auth
params[:state] taken from request; Base64.decode64 is lenient and ignores invalid characters
Marshal.load runs on the decoded bytes with no class allowlist, signature or HMAC, and no size limit
state.inspect is returned, giving the attacker an output channel for the deserialized object

finding.guards_checked: No authentication or authorization middleware in app.rb. No HMAC/signature on the state blob. No class allowlist (Marshal has none built in). No size or type check on params[:state]. Sinatra's default Rack::Protection (HttpOrigin etc.) only rejects browser cross-origin requests that send a foreign Origin header, so a direct non-browser POST is not blocked. Exploitability depends on gadgets in the loaded gem set; no Gemfile or Gemfile.lock is present, so I did not build a working chain. Deployment reachability is unknown.
finding.repro: curl -X POST http://HOST:4567/restore --data-urlencode "state=$(base64 < malicious.marshal)" where malicious.marshal is a Marshal payload built with a gadget chain for the target's gems. Not executed here.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.rb:5 is a bare `post "/restore"` route with no before filter, auth, or signature check. app.rb:6 passes params[:state] through Base64.decode64 straight into Marshal.load with no class allowlist, size limit, or HMAC. app.rb:7 returns state.inspect, so the attacker sees the result. Sinatra's default Rack::Protection only rejects requests with a foreign Origin header, so a plain non-browser POST is not blocked. No Gemfile is present, so I could not check the gem set for gadgets.
verdict.reason: The unauthenticated attacker reaches Marshal.load on attacker-controlled bytes at app.rb:6 with no effective control between source and sink, so unsafe deserialization is confirmed; the trace lines match the file. The "RCE" part is conditional on a gadget chain existing in the deployed gems, which I could not verify, so the critical severity is unproven even though the vulnerability itself is real.

finding.claim: POST /import reflects attacker-chosen JSON object keys into the response body unescaped, and Sinatra's default content type is text/html. This is reflected HTML injection (XSS) on the app origin, conditional on a victim browser being induced to send the POST.
finding.source: app.rb:11 request.body.read, the raw request body, parsed as JSON, so object keys are attacker-controlled
finding.sink: app.rb:12 data.keys.join(",") returned as the HTTP response body with text/html content type

trace.note: raw body read and parsed; Content-Type is not checked, so a text/plain form body that is valid JSON is accepted
keys joined and returned unescaped as the response body

finding.guards_checked: No HTML escaping on the output. No explicit Content-Type header (Sinatra default text/html). Sinatra's default Rack::Protection HttpOrigin is expected to reject cross-origin POSTs that send a foreign Origin header, which blocks the usual form-based delivery; I did not verify this at runtime (Ruby/gem check was blocked by a permission prompt). A same-origin attacker needs an existing XSS elsewhere. Direct attacker POSTs only hit the attacker's own browser. Low severity as a result.
finding.repro: A cross-origin auto-submitting form with enctype=text/plain and name="{\"\":\"" value="=a\"}" would produce body {"":"=a"}. Blocked if HttpOrigin is active. Not executed here.

verdict.guard_found: Sinatra's default Rack::Protection stack (HttpOrigin) is active because app.rb:1-17 never sets `protection` to false. It rejects a POST whose Origin header is foreign, and every cross-origin browser POST carries one. Not verifiable in this directory: there is no Gemfile, so the Sinatra version and its default protections are unconfirmed.
verdict.reason: The trace in app.rb:10-12 is accurate, but a cross-origin form or fetch POST to /import carries a foreign Origin header, which Sinatra's default HttpOrigin protection rejects before the route runs (app.rb has no override). The exploit therefore cannot reach the reflected output, which downgrades this to a non-issue unless protection is disabled in a config not present here.

finding.claim: No request body size limit on /import (and /restore reads params without a limit), and the app runs with Sinatra defaults. Oversized bodies can exhaust memory/CPU, and unhandled exceptions (e.g., JSON::ParserError at line 11, NoMethodError on data.keys at line 12 when the body is an array or scalar, TypeError at line 6) render debug pages with stack traces when RACK_ENV is unset (development). Low severity.
finding.source: app.rb:11 request body size and content; app.rb:6 params[:state]
finding.sink: app.rb:11 JSON.parse of unbounded input; app.rb:12 data.keys on non-hash values; unhandled exceptions at app.rb:6, 11, 12

trace.note: request.body.read has no limit; JSON.parse runs on the full body
data.keys raises NoMethodError for Array/String/Integer JSON roots, which becomes a 500
no set :environment, :show_exceptions or error handler configured, so Sinatra defaults apply

finding.guards_checked: No Rack::Limit or body-size middleware, no rescue blocks, no error handler, no explicit environment setting in app.rb. Deployment config (RACK_ENV, reverse proxy limits) is not in this directory and could mitigate.
finding.repro: POST /import with a multi-GB body, or a JSON array body such as [1], to trigger NoMethodError and a debug page when run in development. Not executed here.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.rb:11 reads request.body.read with no size limit and no Rack::Limit middleware exists in app.rb; app.rb:12 calls data.keys with no type check or rescue; no error handler or set :environment/:show_exceptions appears anywhere in app.rb, so Sinatra's defaults apply. Deployment-level body limits or RACK_ENV settings are outside this directory and could only mitigate, not verify.
verdict.reason: The /import route is anonymous (app.rb:10), reads the full body unbounded (app.rb:11), and calls data.keys on any parsed JSON root (app.rb:12) with no rescue or error handler in app.rb, so a non-hash JSON body produces an unhandled 500 and the Sinatra default development debug page when RACK_ENV is unset. Two caveats: the candidate's line 6 "TypeError" description is loose (nil input to Base64.decode64 raises NoMethodError, and that line is outside the trace), and the DoS impact depends on deployment limits that cannot be seen here.
